newsitem.title: USA: Signet hires J.P. Morgan to conduct branch sale.
newsitem.headline: Signet hires J.P. Morgan to conduct branch sale.

text.p: Signet Banking Corp said Tuesday it hired J.P. Morgan & Co Inc to conduct a sale of 39 branches in parts of Virginia and Maryland.

Earlier Tuesday, Signet announced plans to sell the branches and said it would concentrate resources on the corridor from Baltimore to Washington through Richmond and to the Hampton Roads area of Virginia. Signet is headquartered in Richmond, Va.
Branches for sale are located in Southwest Virginia, a section of Northern Virginia and the Eastern Shore of Virginia and Maryland.

Christopher Oddleifson, executive vice president for consumer financial services, said in a telephone interview that J.P. Morgan has been hired to sell the branches and it is projected the process will take six to nine months. He said the branches have about $800 million in deposits.
Signet said in a news release that it expects to receive a "significant premium" from the sale.
Oddleifson said the strategy was to focus on faster-growing, more densely populated areas where Signet believes it can get a stronger return on its technology investments.
Signet shares were off 1/8 to 33-3/8 at mid-morning.
